name: Whole Masoor Dal Gravy
instructions: Cook the lentils: Pressure cook 120 milliliters whole masoor (brown lentils), rinsed with 360 milliliters water (for pressure cooking lentils) and a pinch of 0.3 teaspoons turmeric powder for 4-5 whistles, or until soft but still holding shape. (Stovetop: simmer covered 15 minutes.)
Temper the spices: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee in a pan. Add 0.5 teaspoons cumin seeds and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Sauté onions: Add 0.5 medium onion, finely chopped and cook until golden brown, about 6 minutes
Add ginger-garlic and chili: Stir in 0.5 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste and 0.5 green chili, slit, cook for a minute until the raw smell goes away.

Cook the tomatoes: Add 1 medium tomato, finely chopped along with 0.5 teaspoons red chili powder, 0.5 teaspoons coriander powder and 0.5 teaspoons salt, to taste. Cook until the tomatoes turn soft and the oil separates, about 8 minutes.

Combine with lentils: Add the cooked 120 milliliters whole masoor (brown lentils), rinsed (with their cooking liquid) into the masala. Pour in 60 milliliters water (to adjust gravy consistency) to adjust consistency and mix well.
Simmer: Let the gravy simmer gently for 10 minutes so the flavors blend, stirring occasionally.
Finish and serve: Sprinkle in 0.3 teaspoons garam masala and 1 tablespoon fresh coriander leaves, chopped. Give it a final stir and serve hot with rice or roti.
dietitian_tip: A simple, healthy whole brown lentil curry with a light onion-tomato gravy - high in protein and fiber, easy weeknight comfort food.

name: Exotic chicken wrap
ingredients: 1 1 multigrain base ragi roti / spinach wrap
instructions: In a bowl marinate the chicken for 1 hr .
Take a pan and shallow pan steam the chicken .
Now take a pan and add a hint of sunflower oil and sauteed onion and capsicum .
Mix the veggies into the pan fried chicken .
Now on a wrap add the chicken and veggies .
Cover the wrap .
Add 1/2 tsp ghee on the pan and heat the wrap
Serve hot .
dietitian_tip: Nutrient dense clinical formulation for Exotic chicken wrap.

name: Healthy Spinach Chicken Shawarma Wrap
ingredients: 300 g boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced
1/2 tsp garlic powder (or 2 cloves minced garlic)
1/2 tsp black and white pepper Pinch of salt
instructions: Marinate the chicken
Mix yogurt, olive oil, spices, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is even better).
Cook the chicken
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Cook chicken for 4-6 minutes per side until browned and fully cooked.
Let rest for a few minutes, then slice.
Make the sauce
Combine all yogurt sauce ingredients and stir until smooth.
Assemble the wraps
Warm the wraps briefly.
Spread yogurt sauce down the center.
Add lettuce, cucumber, tomato, onion, and chicken.
Roll tightly and slice in half.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Healthy Spinach Chicken Shawarma Wrap.

name: Fat-Loss Mango Blueberry Chia Pudding
instructions: Mix chia seeds and almond milk in a jar or bowl and roasted rolled oats.
Stir well, wait 5 minutes, then stir again.
Refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
Add Greek yogurt and mix lightly.
Top with mango and blueberries.
dietitian_tip: Lower sugar, high fiber, filling, and good for calorie control.

name: Healthy Mango Pancakes (Weight-Loss Friendly)
ingredients: 1 egg (or 2 egg whites for lower calories)
instructions: Blend everything into a smooth batter
Cook on a non-stick pan with minimal oil
Make small pancakes for better portion control
Why this works for weight loss
Oats → slow-digesting carbs, keeps you full
Eggs/yogurt → protein reduces cravings
Mango → natural sweetness, no added sugar
What to avoid
No maple syrup or honey (adds unnecessary calories)
Avoid refined flour (maida)
Don't overdo mango-keep it moderate
Smart toppings
A spoon of plain yogurt
Chia seeds or flaxseeds
A few chopped nuts
dietitian_tip: Stick to 2-3 small pancakes + protein topping. Even healthy pancakes can slow weight loss if you overeat.

name: Low-Fat Matcha Latte
ingredients: Use high-protein low-fat milk or add a scoop of unflavored protein powder for a more filling drink.
instructions: Sift the matcha into a cup to avoid clumps.
Add hot water and whisk in a zig-zag motion until frothy.
Heat the low-fat milk and froth if desired.
Pour milk into the matcha mixture.
Sweeten to taste.
Calories (Approx.)
Blend:
1 tsp matcha
1 cup chilled low-fat milk
1-2 tsp vanilla syrup or sweetener
That usually stays under 150 kcal if lightly sweetened.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Low-Fat Matcha Latte.

name: Strawberry Oatmeal Yogurt Jar (Fat-Loss | 1 Serving)
ingredients: Low-fat curd / Greek yogurt - 1/2 cup (120-150 g)
Honey / dates - NOT needed (optional: stevia only)
Water or milk - 2-3 tbsp (to soften oats)
instructions: (Jar Style)
Soak oats with water/milk for 10-15 minutes (or overnight).
In a jar/glass, add:
First layer: soaked oat
Second layer: yogurt
Third layer: chopped strawberries
Sprinkle chia seeds + cinnamon on top.
Mix slightly or keep layered.
Refrigerate overnight or eat fresh.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Strawberry Oatmeal Yogurt Jar (Fat-Loss | 1 Serving).

name: Ragi Uttapam Recipe (Healthy)
ingredients: Water - as needed (to make thick batter)
instructions: In a bowl, mix ragi flour + curd + water to make a thick, lump-free batter.
Add salt and cumin seeds. Mix well.
Let the batter rest for 10-15 minutes (important for softness).
Heat a non-stick tawa and lightly grease it.
Pour a ladle of batter and gently spread (keep it thick like uttapam).
Sprinkle onion, tomato, veggies, ginger, and chilli on top.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.
Cook on medium flame till the base is crisp.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
Serve hot.
dietitian_tip: Coconut chutney (less coconut, more roasted chana) Mint chutney Plain curd or vegetable sambar

name: Strawberry Whey Protein Oatmeal Shake (1 Serving)
ingredients: Low-fat milk or unsweetened almond milk - 200 ml
Chia seeds or flaxseed powder - 1 tsp
instructions: Dry roast oats lightly (optional, improves digestion). Let cool.
Add oats, strawberries, whey protein, milk, seeds, cinnamon to a blender.
Blend until smooth.
Adjust thickness with water if needed.
Consume immediately.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Strawberry Whey Protein Oatmeal Shake (1 Serving).

name: Diabetic-Friendly Tofu Wrap
ingredients: Red chilli flakes - optional, a pinch
Whole wheat roti / multigrain tortilla / ragi roti - 1 piece
Low-fat curd or hung curd dressing - 1 tbsp (mix curd + pinch of salt + roasted jeera + black pepper)
instructions: Prepare tofu filling
Heat 1/2 tsp olive oil.
Add garlic & onions → sauté 1 min.
Add capsicum, cabbage, tomato → cook for 2-3 mins on medium flame.
Add tofu → mix well.
Add turmeric, pepper, chilli flakes & salt.
Cook 3-4 mins until slightly dry.
Switch off flame → add lemon juice & coriander.
Assemble the wrap
Warm the whole-wheat or multigrain wrap.
Spread 1 tbsp curd dressing.
Add the tofu filling.
Roll tightly and toast on a dry pan for 1 minute for crispiness.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Diabetic-Friendly Tofu Wrap.

name: Healthy Paneer Sandwich
ingredients: 2 Whole wheat multigrain roti / multigrain / brown bread - 4 slices
Low-fat curd / hung curd / green chutney - 1-2 tsp (optional, for spread)
Butter / ghee / olive oil - for toasting (optional, 1/2 tsp per sandwich)
Salt, pepper, chaat masala or cumin
instructions: Mix gently to combine. Keep it dry (avoid excess moisture).
To Assemble & Cook:
Spread curd or green chutney on one side of bread (optional).
Add filling on one slice. Cover with another slice.
Toast on tawa/pan with little butter or ghee until golden on both sides.
OR use a sandwich toaster/grill.
Slice & serve hot!
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Healthy Paneer Sandwich.

name: Sprouted Matki Semi-Thick Gravy
ingredients: Red chili powder - 1/2 tsp (adjust to taste)
Water - 1 to 1.5 cups (adjust for semi-thick consistency)
instructions: Cook the matki:
If not already cooked, pressure cook the sprouted matki with a pinch of salt and 1 cup water for 1-2 whistles (or simmer until soft but not mushy).
Temper the spices:
In a pan, heat oil.
Add cumin seeds (and mustard seeds if using). Let them splutter.
Add a pinch of hing.
Add chopped onion and sauté until light golden.
Add ginger-garlic & tomatoes:
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili. Sauté for a minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook until soft and oil starts to separate (or use tomato puree for smoother texture).
Add spices:
Add turmeric, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Mix well and cook for 1 more minute.
Combine matki & shimmer:
Add cooked matki (with water it was cooked in).
Add more water as needed for semi-thick gravy.
Let it simmer for 8-10 minutes on low heat. Mash a few beans lightly to thicken the curry.
Adjust salt and finish:
Check salt. Add more if needed.
Garnish with chopped coriander leaves.
dietitian_tip: Serve with phulka, roti, bhakri, or steamed rice. Pair with a bowl of curd or salad for a balanced meal.

name: Lauki Drumstick Paneer Soup Bowl
instructions: Prepare vegetables:
Peel and cube lauki.
Wash and cut the drumstick into 3-inch pieces.
Cube or crumble paneer.
Cook drumstick and lauki:
In a pressure cooker or pot, add lauki and drumstick pieces with 2 cups of water and a little salt.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles or simmer covered until soft (about 12-15 mins in a regular pot).
Extract drumstick pulp:
Once cooled, take the drumstick pieces, scrape or press out the soft pulp using a spoon.
Discard the outer fibrous shell.
Mash the lauki pieces lightly or blend for a smoother texture.
Sauté aromatics:
In a separate pan, heat oil/ghee.
Add cumin seeds, then sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant (1-2 mins).
Assemble the soup:
Add mashed lauki and drumstick pulp to the pan.
Pour in 1 more cup of water or stock for desired consistency.
Add paneer cubes or crumbles.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Season and finish:
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Turn off the heat.
Stir in lemon juice and coriander leaves.
Serve:
Pour into soup bowls.
Garnish with extra paneer, coriander, or a dash of ghee if desired.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Lauki Drumstick Paneer Soup Bowl.

name: Lemon Coriander Veg Paneer Soup
ingredients: Paneer - 100 g (cut into small cubes or crumbled for a softer texture)
Spring onions or regular onion - 2 tbsp (chopped)
Fresh coriander leaves - 2-3 tbsp (finely chopped, with stems)
Black pepper powder - 1/2 tsp (adjust to taste)
instructions: Prep the veggies: Wash and finely chop all vegetables. Crumble or cube the paneer.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil/ghee in a pan. Add chopped garlic, ginger, and onions. Sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Cook the vegetables: Add carrot, capsicum, and cabbage. Sauté for 2-3 minutes. Do not overcook - keep them slightly crunchy.
Add water or stock: Pour in 3 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil.
Add paneer: Add crumbled or cubed paneer. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Season and simmer: Add salt, pepper, and coriander stems. Simmer for another 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon & coriander: Turn off the heat. Add fresh coriander leaves and lemon juice. Stir well.
Serve hot: Garnish with extra coriander and a lemon wedge if desired.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Lemon Coriander Veg Paneer Soup.

name: Healthy Ragi Veg Soup
ingredients: Mixed vegetables - 1 cup (finely chopped: carrots, beans, capsicum, cabbage, spinach, etc.)
instructions: Prepare the ragi slurry: In a small bowl, mix 2 tbsp ragi flour with 1/2 cup water. Stir well to avoid lumps. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Heat oil or ghee in a pot. Add garlic, ginger, and green chili. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add vegetables: Add the chopped mixed vegetables. Sauté for 2-3 minutes. Add a pinch of salt.
Add water & cook: Pour in 2.5 cups of water. Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the veggies are tender.
Add ragi slurry: Stir the ragi slurry again (it tends to settle). Slowly pour it into the soup while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Simmer: Let it simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring often, until the soup thickens slightly.
Season: Add salt and pepper to taste. Turn off the heat. Add lemon juice if desired.
Garnish & serve: Garnish with chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot!
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Healthy Ragi Veg Soup.

name: Corn and Spinach Soup Bowl
calories: ~150 per bowl Gut-friendly and light on the stomach
ingredients: 1 cup unsweetened almond milk or oat milk/ 1 tbsp corn starch
Salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in a pot for 2 minutes.
Add corn and spinach. Cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add milk/ corn starch and broth, season, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend smooth or leave chunky. Sprinkle with nutmeg.
dietitian_tip: Mildly creamy, rich in fiber and antioxidants

name: Protein-Packed Lentil Veggie Soup
calories: ~180 per bowl High in plant protein and iron
instructions: In a pot, sauté onion, garlic, cumin, and tomato for 3 mins.
Add carrots, lentils, turmeric, and broth.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 mins or until lentils are soft.
Blend partially for a thick texture. Garnish with herbs
dietitian_tip: Hearty, filling, and great for vegetarians

name: Hearty Chicken & Veggie Power Bowl
ingredients: 1/2 cup cooked brown rice or lentils
Optional: A few spinach leaves or parsley to finish
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté onion, garlic, and carrots for 4-5 minutes.
Add green beans, corn/peas, broth, and paprika. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add shredded chicken and cooked rice/lentils.
Simmer for another 5 minutes, season to taste, and serve hot.
dietitian_tip: Filling and balanced with a mix of fiber, protein, and slow-digesting carbs.

name: Green Goddess Chicken Soup Recipe : (Blended Veggie + Chicken)
ingredients: Optional: 1 tbsp 2 tbsp oat milk for creaminess
instructions: In a pot, sauté onion and garlic in olive oil for 2-3 minutes.
Add zucchini, broccoli, spinach, and chicken broth.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Add cooked chicken, and blend about half the soup for a creamy texture (use an immersion blender or regular blender carefully).
Stir everything together, season, and serve.
dietitian_tip: A creamy (but dairy-free!) soup packed with greens and nutrients.

name: Spicy Slim-Down Chicken Soup
ingredients: Fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lime (optional)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, and carrot for 4-5 minutes.
Add bell pepper, tomato, chili flakes, and cumin. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth, add chicken, and bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Serve with chopped cilantro and lime juice.
dietitian_tip: A metabolism-boosting soup with bold flavors and a little kick. Add a little cayenne for more heat!

name: Zesty Lemon Chicken Veggie Bowl
ingredients: 1 cup cooked, shredded chicken breast (grilled or poached)
Salt and black pepper to taste
Optional: 1/4 cup cooked quinoa or brown rice (for extra satiety)
instructions: Sauté the vegetables: In a medium-sized pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds.
Add carrots and zucchini: Stir in the carrots and zucchini. Sauté for another 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add chicken and broth: Pour in the chicken broth and bring the soup to a gentle boil. Lower the heat to a simmer and add the shredded chicken, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Simmer: Let it simmer for about 10-12 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the flavors have melded.
Add lemon: Stir in the lemon juice and zest. Taste and adjust seasoning - add more lemon juice if you like it zesty.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and top with fresh parsley.
dietitian_tip: A light, nourishing soup packed with veggies and a refreshing lemony twist - perfect for a healthy lunch or dinner when you're watching calories but want taste.

name: Cauliflower Peas Sabzi (Normal Healthy Version)
instructions: Clean cauliflower (same as above - hot salted water soak, optional but helpful).
Sauté aromatics:
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds.
Add chopped onions and sauté until translucent or golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and green chili. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes:
Add chopped or pureed tomatoes.
Cook until soft and oil begins to separate.
Add spices:
Turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Mix and cook 1-2 mins.
Add vegetables:
Add cauliflower and peas.
Stir well to coat with masala.
Cover and cook for 10-12 mins, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is tender.
Finish:
Add garam masala and fresh coriander.
Serve with roti or rice
dietitian_tip: With onion and garlic - homestyle and flavorful

name: Cauliflower Peas Sabzi (Healthy Jain Style)
ingredients: Green peas - 1/2 to 3/4 cup (fresh or frozen)
Tomatoes - 2 medium, finely chopped or pureed
instructions: Prep cauliflower:
Rinse florets well and soak in hot salted water for 5 mins to clean. Drain and set aside.
Cook base:
Heat oil or ghee in a pan.
Add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add a pinch of hing, then ginger and green chili. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes:
Add chopped or pureed tomatoes.
Cook until they break down and become paste-like.
Spices:
Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook for 2 minutes.
Add vegetables:
Add cauliflower florets and peas. Mix well.
Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cauliflower is tender.
Finish:
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander.
dietitian_tip: No onion, no garlic, sattvic-friendly

name: Sprouted Matki Sabzi recipe - Jain Style
ingredients: Sprouted matki (moth beans) - 1.5 cups (boiled or pressure-cooked)
Tomatoes - 2 medium, finely chopped or pureed
instructions: Boil the matki:
Pressure cook sprouted matki with a little salt and water (1-2 whistles) or boil in a covered pan until soft but not mushy. Drain excess water if needed.
Prepare the tadka (tempering):
Heat oil or ghee in a pan.
Add cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add a pinch of hing.
Add grated ginger and green chili. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Cook tomatoes:
Add chopped or pureed tomatoes.
Cook until the mixture thickens and the oil/ghee separates slightly.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add sprouted matki:
Add the boiled sprouted matki to the masala.
Mix well and simmer for 4-5 minutes to let flavors absorb.
Finish:
Add garam masala.
Mix and cook for 1 minute.
Garnish with fresh coriander and a dash of lemon juice (optional)
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Sprouted Matki Sabzi recipe - Jain Style.

name: Paneer Capsicum Sabzi recipe (No Onion & Garlic)
instructions: Heat oil. Add cumin seeds and hing.
Add ginger and green chili. Sauté 30 seconds.
Add tomato puree. Cook till it thickens.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt.
Add chopped capsicum. Cook for 3-5 mins.
Add paneer. Mix gently, cook for 2 mins.
Sprinkle garam masala and serve.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Paneer Capsicum Sabzi recipe (No Onion & Garlic).

name: Paneer Capsicum Sabzi
instructions: Heat oil. Add cumin, then onion. Sauté till golden.
Add garlic and green chili. Cook for 1 min.
Add tomatoes. Cook until soft and masala releases oil.
Add turmeric, chili, coriander powder, and salt.
Add capsicum. Cook for 4-5 mins (keep it crunchy).
Add paneer cubes. Mix gently and cook 2-3 mins.
Finish with garam masala
dietitian_tip: A. Normal Style (With Onion & Garlic)

name: Healthy Palak Paneer recipe (Without Onion & Garlic)
instructions: Blanch and puree spinach with green chili and ginger.
Heat oil/ghee, add cumin and a pinch of hing.
Add tomato puree. Cook till thick.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt.
Add spinach puree. Simmer for 3-5 mins.
Add paneer. Simmer for 2 mins.
Finish with garam masala.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Healthy Palak Paneer recipe (Without Onion & Garlic).

name: Healthy Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch spinach: Boil water, add spinach for 1-2 mins, then transfer to cold water. Blend with green chili and a little ginger into a smooth paste.
Cook base: Heat oil. Add cumin, then sauté onion until golden. Add garlic, ginger, tomato. Cook till soft.
Spices: Add turmeric, coriander powder, salt. Cook 2 mins.
Add spinach puree: Mix and cook for 3-5 mins.
Add paneer: Gently mix in paneer cubes and cook 2-3 mins.
Finish: Add garam masala and serve hot
dietitian_tip: A. Normal Style (With Onion & Garlic)

name: No Onion No Garlic Paneer Mushroom Sabzi (Sattvic & Light)
ingredients: Red chili powder - 1/2 tsp (or as per taste)
instructions: Prep:
Wash mushrooms, slice them.
Puree tomatoes.
Grate ginger.
Tempering:
Heat ghee or oil. Add cumin seeds and hing.
Add grated ginger and green chili. Sauté 30 seconds.
Tomato masala:
Add tomato puree. Cook till it thickens and oil/ghee starts to release.
Add turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt.
Cook mushrooms:
Add mushrooms and cook for 6-8 mins until tender.
Add paneer:
Add paneer cubes. Gently mix. Cook 2-3 mins.
Finish:
Sprinkle garam masala.
Garnish with coriander leaves.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for No Onion No Garlic Paneer Mushroom Sabzi (Sattvic & Light).

name: Makhana Porridge
ingredients: 2 cups milk (or dairy-free milk like almond milk)
5-6 black raisins , pinch of saffron strands
A few chopped nuts (almonds, Pistachios) for garnish
instructions: Dry roast the makhana in a pan until it turns slightly golden.
Add milk to the pan and bring it to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let the makhana cook in the milk for 5-7 minutes until soft.
Add black raisins, saffron strands , cardamom powder, and mix well.
Cook for another 2-3 minutes until it thickens slightly.
Garnish with chopped nuts and serve hot.
dietitian_tip: A creamy and nutritious breakfast option for those who want a slightly sweet dish.

name: Makhana Chivda
instructions: Heat ghee or oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, and let them splutter.
Add pumpkin seeds, curry leaves, and roast them for a minute.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, black pepper, and salt. Stir well.
Add the roasted makhana and toss everything together to coat the makhana with the spices.
Cook for 2-3 minutes on medium heat.
Serve as a crunchy snack or breakfast.
dietitian_tip: A crunchy and spicy snack or breakfast dish that's great during fasting.

name: Makhana Ladoo
instructions: Roast the makhana in a pan until crispy. Grind it to a coarse powder in a blender.
Heat ghee in a pan, add grated jaggery, and melt it.
Add the makhana powder, grated coconut, and cardamom powder. Stir well until the mixture comes together.
Once it cools down slightly, shape the mixture into small ladoos.
Garnish with saffron strands if using and let them cool completely before serving.
dietitian_tip: Sweet, energy-boosting ladoos made with makhana, perfect for the fasting season.

name: Rajgira Paneer Paratha
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine rajgira flour, grated paneer, cumin powder, ajwain, and salt.
Gradually add water and knead the mixture into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into small balls and roll each into a small circle using a rolling pin.
Heat a tava or griddle, and cook each paratha with a little ghee or oil until golden brown on both sides.
Serve hot with a side of yogurt or chutney.
dietitian_tip: A filling and protein-rich paratha that's perfect for breakfast.

name: Sabudana and Paneer Salad
instructions: In a bowl, combine the soaked sabudana, chopped cucumber, tomato, and paneer cubes.
Drizzle with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Toss gently and garnish with coriander leaves.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
dietitian_tip: A refreshing, protein-packed salad, perfect for light meals.

name: Rajgira Dosa (Amaranth Flour Dosa)
ingredients: 1/2 cup Samak Rice (Barnyard Millet) or Rice Flour (optional for crispiness)
1 small Potato, boiled and mashed (for softness)
instructions: Prepare the Batter:
In a mixing bowl, combine rajgira flour and rice flour (if using).
Add the boiled and mashed potato, curd, green chilies, cumin seeds, and black pepper.
Mix everything well, adding enough water to create a thin batter (similar to dosa batter consistency).
If using curd, let the batter rest for 20-30 minutes for light fermentation. If you're fasting, you can skip the curd.
Heat the Tawa:
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) on medium heat and grease it lightly with oil or ghee.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin dosa.
Cook the Dosa:
Drizzle a little oil or ghee around the edges.
Cook on medium heat until the bottom side turns golden and crisp.
Flip and cook the other side for a minute or two, depending on the thickness.
Serve:
Once crispy and golden, remove the dosa and serve hot.
Serve with:
Coconut chutney
Peanut chutney
Curd
This Rajgira Dosa is light, nutritious, and perfect for fasting (vrat) or as a gluten-free meal option. Enjoy!
dietitian_tip: A healthy and gluten-free alternative to traditional dosas. Rajgira (also known as Amaranth) is packed with protein and nutrients, making it a great choice for fasting or just a nutritious meal.

name: Grilled Salmon Salad
instructions: Grill or bake the salmon with a little salt and pepper.
In a bowl, combine greens, avocado, tomatoes, and onion.
Flake the cooked salmon over the top.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon or balsamic.
Rich in omega-3, protein, and fiber Time: 15-20 mins
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Grilled Salmon Salad.

name: Homemade Chicken Burger Patty
ingredients: Oil - for fry or air fry -1 tbsp
instructions: Blend all the ingredients in a blender, shape it like a patty, now whisk egg and dip it in the egg then bread crumbs and brush some oil and air fry the chicken patty. You can also shallow fry it with less oil.
Burger preparation :
Take 1 multigrain bun
Spread 1 flat tsp lite mayo
Add the burger patty
Take 1/2 cucumber and tomato place in it
Add 1 leaf of lettuce
Serve .
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Homemade Chicken Burger Patty.

name: Classic Healthy Chicken Salad
instructions: In a bowl, mix Greek yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Stir in the chicken, celery, and onion.
Serve on lettuce, whole-grain toast.
Healthy because: High in protein, no mayo, low-fat Time: 10 minutes
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Classic Healthy Chicken Salad.

name: MB Chocolate oatmeal bowl
instructions: Roast 3 tablespoon rolled oats on a flat pan.
Now add the oats in cow milk and cook on medium flame.
Set it in a bowl, add soaked chia seeds, pumpkin seeds and sliced apple / berries over it.
Serve cold .
(can be refrigerated overnight or served hot).
dietitian_tip: Nutrient dense clinical formulation for MB Chocolate oatmeal bowl.

name: Healthy Paneer Tikka Salad Bowl
ingredients: 2 tbsp thick yogurt (curd or Greek yogurt)
Fresh coriander or mint for garnish
Salt, black pepper, oregano , pinch of cumin powder
(Or use a drizzle of olive oil + lemon instead)
instructions: Marinate the Paneer: Mix yogurt, spices, lemon juice, and salt. Toss in paneer cubes. Let it sit for 10-15 mins.
Cook the Paneer: Grill or pan-sear on medium heat with a little oil until golden and slightly charred (about 6-8 mins).

name: Chicken Whole Masoor Pulao
ingredients: 1 cup whole masoor dal (brown lentils) - soaked 3-4 hrs
1.5 cups basmati rice or brown rice - soaked 20 mins (110g per serve)
Fresh coriander + mint leaves - handful each
1 tbsp ghee or oil (olive or mustard oil works too)
1/2 tsp red chili powder (adjust to taste)
instructions: Soak & Prep
Soak masoor dal for 3-4 hours and rice for at least 20 minutes.
Marinate chicken with curd, salt, turmeric, and ginger-garlic paste for 20 minutes (optional but helps tenderness).
Cook Chicken & Lentils
Heat ghee/oil in a large pressure cooker or heavy pot.
Add whole spices and sauté for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste, sauté for a minute.
Add tomatoes, green chilies, and ground spices. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add chicken and stir for 5-7 mins until lightly browned.
Add soaked masoor dal + 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook:
Pressure cooker: 2 whistles on medium heat
Pot: Simmer covered for 15-20 mins until dal is almost tender
Add Rice & Simmer
Add soaked rice, salt, mint, coriander. Mix gently.
Add water: Use 1.5 to 2 cups water per 1 cup rice (adjust depending on rice type).
Bring to a boil, then lower heat.
Cover and cook until rice is done (12-15 mins).
Final Touch
Let it rest for 5-10 mins before fluffing.
Optional: sprinkle garam masala or lemon juice before serving.
dietitian_tip: Serve with plain curd or raita (mint or cucumber) Side salad: cucumber + carrot + lemon Avoid fried accompaniments to keep it PCOD- and diabetes-friendly

name: Healthy Matki Misal Recipe (Sprouted Moth Beans Curry)

instructions: Sprout the Matki (if not already sprouted): Soak matki overnight, then drain and keep in a covered container for 1-2 days until sprouted.

Make the Masala Base:

Add ginger, garlic, and chopped onions. Sauté until golden.

Simmer for 5-10 minutes until flavors mix well. Add salt as needed.

name: Yellow Jeera- Moong Dal
ingredients: 1 cup yellow moong dal (split yellow lentils)
1 tablespoon ghee (clarified butter) or olive oil
Fresh cilantro (coriander leaves), chopped for garnish.
instructions: Rinse the moong dal under running water until the water runs clear. Soak the dal in water for about 15 minutes. This step is optional but helps to cook the dal faster.
Drain the soaked dal and transfer it to a pressure cooker. Add 2 cups of water and a pinch of turmeric as per given.
Pressure cook the dal for about 3-4 whistles or until it is soft and cooked through. If you don't have a pressure cooker, you can cook the dal in a regular pot, but it will take longer.
Once the pressure has released naturally from the cooker, open the lid and give the dal a stir. Set it aside.
Heat ghee or oil in a large skillet or pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add the minced garlic, grated and slit green chilies to the pan. Sauté until the garlic turns golden brown and aromatic.
Reduce the heat to low and in a pinch add turmeric powder. Stir well to combine the spices.
Add the cooked moong dal to the pan and mix well with the spices .
Add salt to taste and stir everything together.
Simmer the dal for about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld together.
If the dal appears too thick, you can add a little water to achieve your desired consistency. Adjust the seasoning if necessary.
Once the dal is cooked to your liking, turn off the heat. Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro leaves.
Serve the Yellow Jeera Moong Dal hot with rice or roti (Indian flatbread).
Enjoy your Yellow Jeera Moong Dal!

name: Dal Khichdi
instructions: Rinse the rice and lentils (moong dal) together under running water until the water runs clear. Soak them in water for about 30 minutes and then drain.
Heat ghee or oil in a pressure cooker or a deep pot. Add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, and asafoetida (hing). Let them crackle.
Add chopped onions and sauté until they turn golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and mushy.
Now, add turmeric powder, slit green chili, and salt. Mix well.
Add the soaked and drained rice and lentils to the cooker or pot. Mix them with the onion-tomato mixture.
Add enough water to cover the rice and lentils. For a slightly thicker consistency, add 3 cups of water. For a slightly more liquid consistency, add 4 cups of water.

Close the pressure cooker lid and cook for 4-5 whistles on medium heat. If using a pot, cover it with a lid and cook on medium-low heat until the rice and lentils are soft and well-cooked (approximately 20-25 minutes).
Once the pressure is released, open the cooker or pot and gently mix the khichdi. If it appears too thick, you can add some hot water to adjust the consistency.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve hot dal khichdi with yogurt, pickle, or papad.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Dal Khichdi.

name: Veg Pulao
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice under running water until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in water for about 30 minutes and then drain.
Heat ghee or oil in a deep pot or a pressure cooker. Add cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, cloves, green cardamom pods, and bay leaf. Let them sizzle for a few seconds to release their aroma.
Add sliced onions and sauté until they turn golden brown.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and green chili. Sauté for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add diced carrots, capsicum and green peas. Mix well.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder (optional), garam masala, and salt. Stir to coat the vegetables with the spices.
Add the soaked and drained rice to the pot and gently mix it with the vegetables and spices.

Add 2 cups of water. If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook for 1 whistle on medium heat. If using a pot, cover it with a lid and cook on medium-low heat until the rice is cooked and the water is absorbed (approximately 15-20 minutes).
Once the pressure is released or the rice is cooked, fluff it gently with a fork.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Serve the vegetable pulau hot with raita (yogurt dip) and lemon wedges.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Veg Pulao.

name: Vegan Buddha Bowl

Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they become soft and mushy.

If you prefer a creamier consistency, you can add a tablespoon of extra virgin olive oil and whisk it into the sauce.
Once the sauce reaches your desired taste and consistency, transfer it to a jar or container with a lid.

name: Air-Fried Falafel Recipe : (Serves 2 Person)
instructions: In a food processor, combine the cooked chickpeas, parsley, cilantro, onion, garlic, chickpea flour, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, salt, pepper, and baking powder.
Pulse the mixture until it forms a coarse, crumbly texture. Make sure not to overprocess it into a paste.
Transfer the falafel mixture to a bowl and let it rest in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes. This helps the mixture firm up and makes it easier to shape.
Preheat your air fryer to 375°F (190°C).
Remove the falafel mixture from the refrigerator and shape it into small patties or balls, about 1 to 1.5 inches in diameter.
Place the shaped falafel onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Lightly spray the falafel with olive oil spray to promote browning and prevent sticking.
Place the falafel in a single layer in the air fryer basket, making sure they are not touching.
Cook the falafel in the air fryer for about 12-15 minutes, flipping them halfway through, until they are golden brown and crispy.
Once cooked, remove the falafel from the air fryer and let them cool for a few minutes before serving.
Serve the air-fried falafel as a filling for multigrain tortilla, khubus , wrap them in lettuce leaves, cucumber , tomato , tahini sauce, or enjoy them as part of a salad bowl.

name: Methi Multigrain Diet Paratha
ingredients: 1 cup fresh methi (fenugreek) leaves, washed, finely chopped
1-2 green chilies, finely chopped (adjust according to your spice preference)
1 tsp oil or ghee (clarified butter) for the dough
Ghee or oil, for cooking the parathas
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, add the whole wheat flour, chopped methi leaves, chopped onion (if using), green chilies, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, red chili powder (if using), mango powder (1/2 tsp), and salt.
Mix the ingredients well, and then gradually add water to knead the mixture into a smooth and soft dough. You may need approximately 1/2 to 3/4 cup of water for this.

Roll out each ball into a flat disc using a rolling pin on a floured surface. You can make it as thick or thin as you prefer.

name: Basic Quinoa
ingredients: 2 cups water or vegetable/chicken broth (for added flavor)
instructions: Rinse the quinoa: Place the quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse it thoroughly under cold running water. Rub the grains together gently while rinsing to remove any bitterness or saponin residue.

Toast the quinoa (optional): This step is optional but can enhance the nutty flavor of the quinoa. In a dry saucepan over medium heat, add the rinsed quinoa and toast it for a few minutes until it becomes fragrant and slightly golden. Stir it continuously to avoid burning.

Add water or broth: Once the quinoa is rinsed (and optionally toasted), add it to a saucepan along with the water or broth. The standard quinoa-to-water ratio is 1:2, so for 1 cup of quinoa, use 2 cups of water or broth.
Bring to a boil: Place the saucepan over high heat and bring the water to a boil.

Reduce heat and simmer: Once the water boils, reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan with a lid, and let the quinoa simmer. Cook for about 15-20 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed and the quinoa is tender. The grains will become translucent, and you'll see little spirals (germ) around each grain.
Fluff the quinoa: Turn off the heat, but leave the lid on, and let the quinoa rest for 5 minutes. Then, fluff the quinoa gently with a fork to separate the grains.
Your basic quinoa is now ready to serve as a nutritious side dish or as a base for salads, bowls, and other dishes.

name: Green gram dosa recipe: (4 servings )

name: Whole Masoor Veg Pulao (Brown Lentil Pulao)
ingredients: 1 cup Basmati rice (or brown rice for added fiber)
1 cup veg (carrot, cauliflower , french beans ) diced
1 bay leaf, 2 green cardamoms, 1 small cinnamon stick, 2-3 cloves
2 1/2 cups water (adjust based on the rice and dal)
instructions: Rinse and soak lentils and rice: Wash the whole masoor dal and Basmati rice separately under running water. Soak them both in water for about 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat oil or ghee: In a large pan or pressure cooker, heat the oil or ghee over medium heat.
Sauté whole spices: Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and cloves. Sauté until the spices release their aroma (about 30 seconds).
Sauté onions and ginger-garlic: Add the sliced onions and cook until golden brown. Add grated ginger, minced garlic, and green chili (if using), and sauté for 1-2 minutes.

Add tomatoes and veggies: Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they soften. Then, add the diced carrots, cauliflower , french beans, peas, and potato (if using). Sauté for 2-3 minutes until the vegetables are slightly tender.
Add spices: Sprinkle in turmeric powder, cumin powder, and salt. Mix everything well and cook for another minute.
Add rice and lentils: Now, add the drained rice and soaked masoor dal to the pan. Gently mix them with the sautéed vegetables and spices.

Add water and cook: Pour in 2 1/2 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Lower the heat, cover the pan, and cook on a simmer for about 20-25 minutes, or until the rice and lentils are tender, and the water is absorbed. (If using a pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle and then let it rest until the pressure releases naturally).
Finish with garam masala: Once the rice and lentils are fully cooked, sprinkle garam masala over the pulao and gently mix.
Garnish and serve: Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve the pulao hot with yogurt or cucumber salad.
dietitian_tip: High fiber & balanced nutrients for Whole Masoor Veg Pulao (Brown Lentil Pulao).

Sauté onions and tomato : Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until they turn translucent. Add the diced tomato sauté for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, soft and mushy.
Add spices: Add the turmeric powder, cumin powder, red chili powder (if using), coriander powder, and salt. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes until the spices blend with the tomatoes.
Add crumbled paneer: Now, add the crumbled paneer to the pan and gently mix with the spices and veggies. Cook for 3-4 minutes, allowing the paneer to absorb the flavors.
Garnish and serve: Turn off the heat and garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.

name: Curd Kadhi

instructions: Prepare the curd-besan mixture: In a mixer, add the curd and besan together until smooth and there are no lumps.

Cook the kadhi: Transfer the curd-besan mixture to a deep pan. Add turmeric powder and keep stirring constantly until it boils. Heat it over medium heat while continuously stirring to prevent curdling. Bring it to a boil, then reduce the heat to low when the kadhi thickens slightly.
Prepare the tempering (tadka): In a small pan, heat safflower oil. Add beaten garlic cloves and let them turn slightly golden brown.
Turn the flames low and add cumin seeds, mustard seeds, 1 tsp zeera, and curry leaves. Let the seeds splutter and the curry leaves crisp up.
Add the tempering to the kadhi: Pour the prepared tempering over the simmering kadhi. Stir well to combine the flavors. Let the kadhi simmer for another 2-3 minutes.
Garnish and serve: Turn off the heat and garnish the kadhi in a bowl.
Serve the Curd Kadhi hot with steamed rice, brown rice, or whole wheat chapati.

Sauté Vegetables:

Combine Ingredients:

Finish and Serve:

name: Sprouted green Moong cottage cheese Salad Bowl
ingredients: Pinch of chaat masala (optional, for extra flavor)
instructions: 1: Sprout the Moong Beans
Rinse the moong beans thoroughly. Soak them in water overnight (or for 8 hours).

Drain the water and leave the soaked beans in a container or a muslin cloth for 1-2 days to sprout. Rinse and drain them 1-2 times a day. The sprouts should be ready when tiny sprouts appear from the beans.
2: Prepare the Salad
In a large mixing bowl, add the sprouted moong beans.
Add the chopped cucumber, tomato, onion (optional), chopped 2-3 leaves, iceberg lettuce, and green chilies (if using). Toss everything together gently.
3: Make the Dressing
In a small bowl, mix the lemon juice, olive oil, cumin powder, black salt, black pepper, and chaat masala (optional). Drizzle this dressing over the salad and toss everything together to combine.
4: Garnish and Serve
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Grate 40g of cottage cheese or top it with 40g grilled cottage cheese cubes and serve.
